newsitem.title: CANADA: INSTANT VIEW - Canada Jan unemployment.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Canada Jan unemployment.

text.p: Following are reactions to unemployment data released by Statistics Canada on Friday. Statistics Canada said Canada's unemployment rate remained flat at 9.7 percent from December.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast, on average, unemployment to fall to 9.6 percent in January.

Mark Mullins, chief economist, Midland Walwyn Capital Inc - "Not a heck of a lot of change here to be honest. Now, we are following a very strong report in December so people shouldn't be surprised if we take a little bit of a pause.

Mullins - "We have got a very, very strong track on the help wanted index. The last time we had this kind of strong track was going into 1994 and we had an exceptionally strong year for job growth that year."

Steve Saldanha, economist, Canada Trust - "I think if you look at the headline numbers, it may seem a bit disappointing with only minor job gains of around 5,000. But if you scratch the surface and look a little deeper, you see that this report is not that tepid.
"In fact, you had a job gain full-time of 32,000.
Saldanha - "That's the kind of indicator that we look for going forward to be the underpinning of a consumer renaissance this year."

Paul Ferley, assistant chief economist, Bank of Montreal - "The employment numbers are still giving indications of employment strengthening. I am a little bit disappointed that we are not seeing stronger gains but we have come off three months of employment growth and the January data suggest that we are managing to hold onto those gains. As well, there was a strong increase in full-time employment.
Ferley - "That was offset by a fairly sizeable drop in part-time.

"So, we're not seeing as much evidence of strength in overall activity -- GDP growth -- translating as yet in terms of labor market conditions. Our view though is that that will start showing up in greater strength going forward.
"We are expecting that in subsequent months we are going to start seeing more solid signs of employment growth and the unemployment rate moving lower."
